shoal_e17_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Four, He Ming brought a supplier's replacement-order account to the permitted receiving table. Three workers had completed accepted unloading and were still waiting for the eighteen copper due to them. The supplier said the carrier cost had exhausted the available portion. He Ming wanted the actual charges examined. Yue's earlier receiving arrangement would determine which statements could be used publicly and which people must be asked again.

shoal_e17_public_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_01.text: The named joint statement remained available under its actual public consent. Its receiving dates and the carrier's published reply could be compared without opening a private appointment file. Two eligible workers had each received six copper after the earlier challenge. Two other claims remained unresolved. He Ming laid out that history before asking whether the same supplier's present replacement order had treated a canceled carrier day as if it had actually traveled.

shoal_e17_public_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_02.text: One original signatory declined to sign a new statement. Her prospective commission had been withdrawn after the earlier public dispute, and she would not pretend the cost had vanished because two payments arrived. He Ming respected the refusal. The existing public statement remained within its offered scope, but a new claim required its own consenting people. Yue kept the refusal out of any accusation that a worker had ceased caring about the others.

shoal_e17_public_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_03.text: A second signatory agreed to describe his actual carrier receiving again at the new meeting. He wanted the date and scope precise enough that nobody borrowed his name for a different journey. Han prepared the permitted extract from the public source. The worker read it and corrected a word that implied he had seen the truck loaded. He had seen its return, which was useful evidence and a narrower one.

shoal_e17_public_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_04.text: The current replacement-order source was a separate ninety-six-copper supplier appropriation. It reserved eighteen for three workers' accepted unloading, forty-eight for a quoted carrier-and-packing scope, twenty for qualified stock inspection, and ten for ordinary administration. The old wage bond and Yue's two-hundred-forty-copper receiving fund had not paid it. He Ming wanted the labor eighteen settled from this actual order, not another rescue of an unsupported supplier figure.

shoal_e17_public_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_05.text: The published carrier reply showed how to request the present trip's own receipt. It did not certify every later charge. He Ming sent a current consented request under the workers' small meeting allocation. The carrier's actual receiver agreed to bring the new trip record on the named date. Public source access had shortened the path to asking that question. It had not made the answer exist before the receiver arrived.

shoal_e17_public_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_06.text: At the market, a supplier clerk complained that the workers were turning every discrepancy into a public trial. The worker who had lost the commission answered that public silence had not made his own loss less public. Another worker said he preferred a quiet settlement if it actually paid. Their disagreement survived standing on the same side of the table. He Ming asked them to decide which current statements each actually offered.

shoal_e17_public_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_07.text: Yue was invited to explain the ordinary receiving she had witnessed, without representing all workers or certifying hidden events. She accepted one finite meeting interval after her paid term closed. A public source could make her own role easier to describe. It also made it easier for strangers to put every word she said into a story about cultivation. She asked Han to preserve the narrow title receiving witness on the current notice.

shoal_e17_public_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_08.text: The supplier's manager asked to move the meeting behind a closed door. The current signatories considered it and declined because their accepted public evidence already concerned a public claim. They still left private household information out. The manager could bring actual accounts and dispute their figures. He could not require a worker's family history as the price of answering whether a carrier had traveled on a charged date.

shoal_e17_public_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_09.text: The signatory who refused new participation came to Yue's table later with a separate routine receipt. They did not discuss the meeting. Her ordinary paid work continued, though the lost commission had narrowed it. Yue received the offered receipt in its proper scope and left the woman free to go. An earlier choice could create access without turning every person affected by it into a permanent public witness.

shoal_e17_public_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_10.text: He Ming printed the current meeting questions with the actual consenting names and no others. The public statement's earlier two unsettled claims remained marked pending, rather than folded into the new eighteen-copper unloading claim. Four different items did not become one victory because the word supplier appeared in each. The workers wanted present wages, and some also wanted older answers. The meeting would need to hear which question it could actually resolve.

shoal_e17_public_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_11.text: At the door, the returning carrier receiver read the notice and asked that its own scope be added. It would describe one actual replacement-order trip and one canceled appointment. It had no power to determine every worker's entire wage history. He Ming added the line before the room opened. Clearer evidence could frustrate a dramatic accusation while still support a concrete repayment. He preferred a sum the workers could actually receive.

shoal_e17_public_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_public_12.text: Yue left the public extracts in their authorized custody and took only her own offered speaking notes home. The workers had a visible path into the meeting, with a real social cost already borne by some of them. No lost commission reappeared because current evidence was easier to read. Tomorrow's account challenge would be a new attempt built on the source they had actually chosen to make available.

shoal_e17_private_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_01.text: The earlier three appointments remained restricted to their offered receiving scope. One checked six-copper payment had been made; two claims were still unresolved. No joint public statement had been received at that window. He Ming could not put appointment extracts on a wall because a later labor question now needed evidence. Yue explained which current permissions existed and which people would have to be asked for a new consented use.

shoal_e17_private_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_02.text: One appointment holder declined any public release. She was willing to answer a narrow question privately through the same accepted receiving route. Another agreed to permit a current dated extract after reading its exact wording. The third was away on actual paid work and could not be reached before the meeting's first proposed date. Their different answers were not obstacles to be overcome by saying the group needed solidarity.

shoal_e17_private_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_03.text: He Ming moved the meeting to a later accepted window so the actual current carrier record could be requested. The delay cost the waiting workers another period without their unloading wages. It preserved a process that did not steal somebody else's private statement. He asked whether they wanted an interim payment request from the uncontested labor line. All three accepted that narrower action while the carrier question remained under examination.

shoal_e17_private_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_04.text: The replacement order itself was a separate ninety-six-copper supplier source. Eighteen reserved the three workers' performed unloading, forty-eight covered a quoted carrier-and-packing scope, twenty paid qualified stock inspection, and ten ordinary administration. It had no claim on the old wage bond or Yue's current receiving appropriation. The supplier could not point to another account's empty line as proof this accepted labor had no money behind it.

shoal_e17_private_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_05.text: The one new permitted extract established a date for the earlier appointment holder's actual receiving, not a view of the replacement trip. Han used it to identify the correct carrier office and sent a current request for that office's own record. Private source access had produced a slower and narrower path. It still gave the workers a usable question without publishing the contents of all three original appointments.

shoal_e17_private_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_06.text: The supplier's clerk offered to settle quietly if the workers withdrew every present question. He Ming asked which sum would actually be paid and whether the offer required surrendering the still-valid older claims. The clerk had authority to discuss only the new order's eighteen copper. The workers could accept that payment without pretending two unresolved earlier claims had ceased to exist. They asked for the offer in terms the clerk could actually authorize.

shoal_e17_private_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_07.text: At the market, one waiting worker said privacy had become an expensive courtesy. Another said a public name could cost work too. They disagreed without either possessing the other person's risk. Yue listened while each named what the other had already overlooked. She asked which current receiving they wanted completed. The answer was the uncontested wage request now and a properly sourced carrier question at the later meeting.

shoal_e17_private_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_08.text: Yue accepted an offered finite role explaining the receiving procedure after her current paid term closed. She would identify actual permissions, not disclose sealed appointments. The supplier manager wanted her to certify that no public complaint existed and therefore no wrong had occurred. She refused that inference. A private process could hold a real dispute. The absence of a wall notice was not proof that a worker had been paid.

shoal_e17_private_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_09.text: The carrier receiver accepted the current record request and named its own meeting scope. It could describe one actual replacement trip and a canceled appointment, with the proper charges. It could not replace absent appointment holders or speak for their households. He Ming gave the workers the named date. The delay remained real, but the evidence arriving then would come from a person who had actually managed the carrier's record.

shoal_e17_private_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_10.text: The appointment holder who declined publication brought a separate ordinary receipt to Yue during the last paid week. Yue received it without asking again whether she might change her mind for the group's benefit. Her refusal was already an answer. The ordinary receipt was work within its own scope. A person could keep a private claim and still participate in the harbor's everyday exchanges without becoming a public symbol of caution.

shoal_e17_private_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_11.text: Han prepared the meeting sheet with only the new consented extract and the replacement order's offered figures. The two older unsettled claims remained pending in their proper restricted receiving. He Ming disliked how much was absent from the sheet and respected why. A narrower current challenge could still secure eighteen copper of actual wages. It did not have to become an invented complete history to deserve the workers' time.

shoal_e17_private_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_private_12.text: Yue left the restricted sources where their owners had authorized them to remain. Her own speaking notes described procedure and current facts within her offered role. The meeting would start later than a public receiving might have allowed. Nobody called the delay harmless. It was part of the source path she had helped preserve, beside one earlier six-copper payment and people whose private words still belonged to them.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_01.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Five, the named clerk closed the performed portion of Yue's receiving appointment. Thirty actual four-hour shifts, two readers' accepted reports, and current materials and messages were matched to their own source. The ordinary public office retained pending requests outside this finite scope. Yue returned the room key she had used during her shifts. She did not leave a promise that anyone could summon her back for free.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_02.text: The supplier released nine copper of the eighteen due unloading wages that afternoon, three to each consenting worker against actual performed labor. The remaining nine stayed due under the order. The partial payment helped and was not the completed settlement. He Ming recorded the actual receiving without praising the supplier for paying half as though a full agreed wage had been a charitable aspiration.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_03.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Six, Yue received the final twenty-five-copper weekly settlement. All one hundred fifty under the new receiving appointment had now been earned and actually paid. The sixty-copper readers' line, eighteen-copper tags and closures, and twelve-copper messages also closed on their performed accepted scopes. Two hundred forty funded this particular completed work. It did not purchase every future correction the harbor might need.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_04.text: The workers funded their account meeting from a new twenty-four-copper dues allocation they had actually accepted. Twelve paid two ordinary account readers six each, six the finite clerk interval, and six permitted receiving messages. It paid no medical treatment or road kit. Yue accepted no fee for her separately offered witness interval. The workers could use ordinary skilled help without making their entire claim depend on a cultivator's judgment.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_05.text: Han read the current replacement order before the meeting opened. The forty-eight-copper quoted carrier-and-packing line assumed two twelve-copper carrier appointments, twelve of packing, eight of tags, and four of messages. A quote was not a record that both appointments had traveled. The actual carrier receiver would have to identify the performed journey and the canceled date under its accepted cancellation clause.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_06.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Seven, Bo completed his sixth four-copper rehabilitation session. Twenty-four copper of the session line had now been used. The practitioner checked actual movement and current symptoms before allowing the next ordinary progression. Bo still could not perform his former heavy hauling. He wanted an answer about whether the shop could keep a worker longer. The practitioner could address his body, not promise the business a profitable month.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_07.text: Bo and Jin discussed the business after the appointment. She wanted the apprentice paid for every actual accepted hour. Bo agreed and then worried aloud that the narrower shop might not afford enough hours. Jin preferred that worry to a promise made before they counted. They did not ask Yue to create money by calling the apprentice's loyalty priceless. A valued worker could still need a wage the business could actually pay.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_08.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Eight, the final five-copper restricted-income payment reached Bo. All thirty had now been received over six actual dates. The finite line closed without becoming an ongoing salary. Two future rehabilitation sessions remained accepted within their separate line, and the household retained current ordinary care routes. The ending of one support payment left a real gap for Bo and Jin to address themselves.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_09.text: The account room opened later that day at its accepted hours. The manager sat beside the supplier clerk who had prepared the disputed figure. Three unloading workers sat opposite, with He Ming near the doorway. Yue used the ordinary witness chair offered for her narrow role. The carrier receiver brought its own current records. Nobody in the room had authority to speak for every supplier or every worker in the port.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_10.text: The first worker described the actual unloading date, scope, and accepted six-copper wage. The second confirmed her own work without claiming she had watched every minute of his. The third produced his receiving line and the supplier's acceptance. Nine had already been paid among them. Their current request was the remaining nine and an explanation of why the completed labor line had been held behind an uncertain carrier figure.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_11.text: The manager said the fire had made every account difficult. A worker answered that difficulty explained some delay and did not complete an unpaid wage. The manager began to discuss the port's total losses. He Ming returned to the ninety-six-copper order on the table. A large true hardship could still be irrelevant to whether a small accepted source contained money due for work already done.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_12.text: The carrier receiver identified one performed twelve-copper journey. The second appointment had been canceled before its ordinary dispatch threshold and carried a six-copper cancellation charge under the actual accepted clause. Eighteen had been received by the carrier, not twenty-four. The truck had not traveled on the canceled date. It did not claim otherwise or repay a fee it had never taken.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_13.text: The supplier clerk looked at the account she had prepared and found the quoted twenty-four copied into the completed-charge column. She had used the planned schedule while sorting several orders after the fire. The current record did not show a secret extra journey. It showed a six-copper overstatement inside the supplier's bookkeeping. That difference mattered to the repair: the unused six remained with the order's custodian, not in a carrier's pocket.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_14.text: One worker wanted to call the clerk a thief. Another asked whether calling her that would help identify where the money actually stood. The clerk had made a serious error and the manager had relied on it to hold wages. The current evidence did not establish that either had taken the six for private use. He Ming asked the account readers to state the proven error and leave an unsupported accusation out.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_15.text: The manager objected that correcting six did not explain why nine remained unpaid. He was right about the arithmetic and wrong about the obligation. The eighteen-copper labor line had been separately reserved. Its second half had been held by an internal instruction that treated uncertain total costs as grounds to delay labor. That instruction had no accepted term allowing the manager to replace a completed wage with an indefinite future promise.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_16.text: Yue explained the ordinary receiving dates she had actually witnessed and stopped there. She did not testify about a carrier's hidden route or the supplier clerk's intentions. A worker asked whether her six pairs made her more certain. She said the records and firsthand people supplied the certainty available here. Her body had not been present on the canceled road. The question returned to the actual accepted wage source.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_17.text: The two account readers independently matched the current invoices, the source allocation, and the payments already received. They agreed the labor eighteen was due for completed work. They also agreed the actual carrier-and-packing scope totaled forty-two: eighteen carrier, twelve packing, eight tags, four messages. Their agreement came from the records they had examined, not from harmonizing a quarrel until nobody looked upset.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_18.text: The manager authorized the remaining nine from the still-reserved labor line under his actual source authority. Three copper reached each worker against the balance of their accepted six. All eighteen unloading wages were now actually paid. The workers signed receiving for what they had received and did not sign away older separate claims. The room had resolved a current item without pretending every unfinished dispute had vanished.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_19.text: Qualified stock inspection had actually used its twenty-copper accepted scope on its proper work dates. The ten-copper ordinary administration line also matched performed work. With labor eighteen and carrier-and-packing forty-two, the ninety-six source closed at ninety actually spent and six unused returned to its named owner. The return did not become Lin's reward. The carrier had earned its cancellation charge under the actual clause and retained it.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_20.text: The supplier clerk asked whether she could personally pay the workers something extra to apologize. They declined a casual exchange that might later look like closing other claims. One asked for the revised account copy and a future process that did not hold their wages behind unrelated uncertainty. The clerk could help prepare a correction. The manager would need to accept any new procedure through his own actual authority.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_21.text: He Ming proposed a simple separation: performed labor receiving should be checked from its own reserved line before uncertain carrier costs were settled. The supplier manager disliked the extra step and agreed to a bounded trial on two new orders, with named ordinary staffing. The trial did not rewrite the old contract or guarantee every later manager would follow it. It created an actual next test whose results could be checked.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_22.text: A worker asked whether the present room would publish every source. The clerk described what each owner had consented to offer and which earlier records remained restricted. The current corrected order could be circulated under its own accepted terms. Private household details and unoffered statements stayed outside. A visible payment did not buy permission to make the whole port's paperwork public.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_23.text: The manager left before the workers finished speaking among themselves. He had another actual appointment and did not stay to receive a scene of reconciliation. The workers counted their three remaining copper each. One wanted to spend hers on food immediately; another saved his for a road fare. Their differing choices were part of receiving wages. He Ming did not ask them to show that the money had been used wisely enough.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_24.text: Outside, the clerk caught up with Yue and said she had been afraid of being made the fire's convenient villain. Yue said the corrected figure needed to remain visible and the accusation needed actual evidence. The clerk asked whether that meant Yue trusted her. Yue answered that trust about future work would grow from future work. They could finish one clear account without requiring each other to settle every feeling beside the door.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_25.text: The workers' six-copper message line completed actual permitted receiving and dispatch for the meeting. The readers and clerk received their respective fees after the accepted work. Twenty-four had funded the bounded account challenge. He Ming posted its closing figures with the current consented result. He did not add the port's missing tool value as another sum the meeting had recovered.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_26.text: At the inn that evening, Yue heard strangers praise the workers for winning against all the suppliers. She described the actual corrected order only when asked within its offered public scope. One manager and one source were not all suppliers, and two older unresolved claims remained in their proper processes. The listeners found that less satisfying than the broad story. Accuracy could disappoint people who wanted a single ending.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_27.text: The next morning the first worker thanked He Ming, then argued that the proposed trial was too modest. He Ming said the manager had accepted only two actual orders, and a larger proposal would need its own consent and staffing. The worker decided to ask others whether they wanted to fund a wider campaign. He could be grateful for the present wages and want more change afterward.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_28.text: The second worker declined that new campaign. She had an actual family journey to prepare and did not want her name carried forward automatically. Her completed unloading wage remained hers. He Ming removed her from the proposed future list when she asked. Solidarity could include a finite accepted action and a departure from the next one without turning the person into an enemy of those who stayed.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_29.text: Han took down the special meeting notice after its accepted period. A visitor arriving late asked why he had missed it. Han pointed to the posted dates and offered the current permitted result. The visitor wanted to argue about the old whole-port wage bond. That remained a separate source and process. The room had not gained authority over it by successfully correcting six copper in a new replacement order.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_30.text: Yue spent the afternoon after her offered meeting interval repairing a loose seam in her own sleeve. She used an ordinary needle and thread she had already bought, working slowly enough that her elbow remained comfortable. A cultivation stage did not make sewing beneath her. The sleeve's repaired edge was uneven. It would hold for the intended ordinary use, and she could improve it another day if she cared enough.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_31.text: Song passed the inn's public table with a musician and stopped to examine the sleeve only when Yue offered it. She said the stitching was honest. Yue asked whether that meant ugly. Song said it meant visible, which might be useful if the sleeve wished to remember its history. The musician refused to take a side and asked where the innkeeper kept the pepper. Their conversation moved on before it became advice.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_32.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_32.text: The corrected supplier account did not stop all wage disputes. A different worker came with a different order whose proof had not been offered. The ordinary office gave her its current receiving process. He Ming could help if she asked within his available hours. Yue's finished paid appointment remained finished. The town needed institutions and people with ongoing defined roles, not one woman whose every useful act made the next claim personally hers.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_33.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_33.text: On Day Three Hundred Sixty-Four, Bo completed his seventh four-copper rehabilitation session. Twenty-eight copper of the thirty-two session line had actually been used, leaving the final accepted visit future. He could walk a limited distance with his staff under the current plan. The practitioner kept the distance and load restrictions clear. Improvement was real; the former heavy hauling remained unqualified.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_34.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_34.text: Jin watched him return from the permitted short walk and asked how the leg felt after rest, not just at the moment he wanted praise. He admitted a soreness he had intended to minimize. They used the current ordinary contact instructions rather than assuming effort must overcome it. The practitioner addressed the report within the actual care arrangement. Bo disliked another cautious day and preferred it to an avoidable setback once the discomfort had settled.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_35.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_35.text: Yue visited only for the short ordinary interval they offered. Bo wanted to hear about the paid workers, not every private source. She described the current order's actual settlement within its public terms. He asked whether the clerk would still have a job. Yue said she did not know the employer's future decision. He nodded. A corrected error did not supply an outsider with knowledge of every consequence afterward.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_36.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_36.text: Bo showed her the fastening drawers now labeled by the apprentice in a hand clearer than his own. He was paying for fewer hours than the apprentice would have liked, but the accepted hours were actually paid. The business remained smaller. Yue asked about a peculiar hooked piece on the table, and he explained its ordinary use with enough animation that Jin quietly left them to argue about tools for a while.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_37.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_37.text: At home that night, Yue reviewed her own current options. The meeting had completed the last future use of the earlier receiving arrangement in this account challenge. Public and private paths had produced different access, costs, and delays; neither gave her an indefinite witness post. The surviving source rights remained with their actual owners. Her next work would require a new choice, and Song had offered only a conversation about hers.

shoal_e17_source_rejoin_38.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_source_rejoin_38.text: On Day Three Hundred Sixty-Five, the weather cleared enough for the quay's small ordinary performances to return outdoors. Vendors took their actual permitted places, and the musicians kept clear of the carrier lane. Yue heard Song rehearse a final line she had not heard before. It was sharper than the old ending. She wanted to know whether Song would sing it publicly and understood that wanting to know was not the same as being invited to decide.

shoal_e17_town_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_01.text: During the days after the account meeting, the quay held its ordinary summer mending fair. Stallholders paid their actual permitted place fees, and customers brought household objects too modest for the partnership's formal schedules. One woman wanted a cracked comb made usable, another a basket handle, another advice about whether a chair was worth repairing. Yue walked through with her own sleeve already mended and no reason to pretend every artisan's skill was hers.

shoal_e17_town_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_02.text: A basket maker asked a customer how much weight she normally carried before quoting for the handle. The customer said whatever fit. He showed the weakened rim and asked again. They eventually named an ordinary intended load. He could make a repair suitable for that use, or she could buy a different basket. An object did not become safer because its owner disliked being asked about the work it actually had to do.

shoal_e17_town_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_03.text: At the next stall, a comb mender declined the cracked piece after examining its teeth. The owner was offended until he showed why a repair would cost more than a plain new comb without being as sound. She still kept the old one because it had belonged to her mother. He did not mock that choice. She could retain a keepsake while buying a different object for ordinary daily use.

shoal_e17_town_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_04.text: He Ming arrived carrying a stool with a wobbling leg. The stallholder recognized him and offered to fix it free because he had helped workers obtain wages. He asked the ordinary price instead. The stallholder was free to give a gift, but He Ming did not want the fair's entire labor becoming gratitude to a man whose work already had its own agreed support. They settled on a small actual repair charge.

shoal_e17_town_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_05.text: Yue watched the stool's ordinary test after the repair. The craftsperson loaded it within its intended household use and checked the joins independently of the owner sitting down too soon. Nothing glowed. The stool became useful because someone knew wood, had appropriate materials, and stopped when a joint needed another turn. Yue liked that the work could be precise without borrowing the vocabulary of cultivation.

shoal_e17_town_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_06.text: A performer at the fair wore a mask painted as a pompous supplier. The crowd laughed when he counted the same sack three times. Rong Sui stood at the edge and laughed once, then looked uncomfortable. The performer was not naming the current corrected order as factual evidence. He was making a broad comic figure. Yue hoped the audience could enjoy it without concluding every supplier at the quay had committed the same error.

shoal_e17_town_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_07.text: Song watched the mask performance with a professional interest that did not require admiration. She disliked the easy ending in which one clever worker shamed the entire town. The performer said easy endings brought coins. She said they could, then asked whether he wanted to try a harder verse. He declined that day. His art remained his, and her opinion did not compel him to make it more like hers.

shoal_e17_town_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_08.text: A child dropped a coin between the planks near the stall. The fairkeeper stopped traffic through that small section while an ordinary worker retrieved it with a suitable hook from the safe side. Yue did not reach overhead or pry the structure with qi. The coin returned, and the child guarded it with exaggerated suspicion afterward. The actual brief closure delayed several customers and gave the retrieved coin a story larger than its value.

shoal_e17_town_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_09.text: The child spent it on a paper boat. He wanted to sail it in the public trough until the keeper explained that the trough supplied drinking water for working animals. He chose a shallow basin the paper seller had actually provided for demonstrations instead. The boat lasted two circuits and then sagged. He demanded a vessel that would never sink. The seller said that was outside the ordinary paper boat's price and abilities.

shoal_e17_town_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_10.text: Yue laughed because the answer resembled many adult conversations at the receiving room. The child did not find it funny. He took the softened boat home anyway, perhaps to dry it or perhaps because leaving it behind felt worse. His father thanked the seller for the actual basin and steered him clear of a laden cart. The fair continued without requiring anyone to turn the failed boat into a lesson the child must appreciate.

shoal_e17_town_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_11.text: At an ordinary food stall, Yue used her own received money for a small bowl, checking the price before ordering. She had no paid shift that afternoon and still had ordinary costs. The seller offered extra broth because the pot was nearly empty. She accepted it as an actual small gift, not a grant for future meals. Across the lane, a musician counted his earnings before deciding whether he could buy the same supper.

shoal_e17_town_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_12.text: Han came late after closing his current office hours. He wanted his old coat clasp repaired and refused to discuss account figures while the craftsperson measured its pin. He Ming teased him about leaving numbers at work. Han said the numbers would survive an evening without him if properly filed. He did not dislike helping people. He disliked a town forgetting that a helpful clerk also needed a coat that closed in rain.

shoal_e17_town_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_13.text: The craftsperson completed the clasp repair under the accepted price and showed Han how it seated. Han paid after inspecting it. He Ming tried it once with permission and declared it much too solemn for a summer fair. Han said he would buy a frivolous clasp when the solemn one no longer kept weather out. Their ordinary friendship had arguments that no institutional minutes needed to preserve.

shoal_e17_town_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_14.text: As evening cooled, stallholders began packing under the fair's actual closing time. A late customer wanted a basket repaired immediately. The maker named his next accepted hours and refused to rush the join while removing his stall. The customer left annoyed and later returned to ask about tomorrow. A clear ending could lose a sale and still make the work more reliable for the people who actually completed it.

shoal_e17_town_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_15.text: The fairkeeper returned the borrowed ordinary demonstration basin to its owner after emptying it in the proper place. The paper boats still floating belonged to their buyers or to the seller's unsold stock. Yue helped move one light empty stool with the owner's permission and within her current ordinary limits. She did not become the fair's unappointed porter because she had begun helping. Other stallholders completed their own actual packing.

shoal_e17_town_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_16.text: At the lane's end, the corrected-order clerk met one unloading worker without either expecting a public ceremony. The worker asked whether the next trial order had a separate labor receiving line. The clerk said the manager had accepted the planned form but no work under it had yet been performed. The worker thanked her for the actual answer. Their future trust would need more than that one useful exchange.

shoal_e17_town_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_17.text: Yue walked home beside a couple arguing about the comb they had kept. One wanted it hung as a keepsake; the other wanted it wrapped so the remaining teeth would not break. They found a third idea and fell silent. The quarrel had nothing to do with her next road, and that was part of its comfort. A town was not merely the collection of disputes a visitor happened to help receive.

shoal_e17_town_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_18.text: She slept poorly that night despite the pleasant evening. Her shoulder ached in the old ordinary way, and she adjusted her position rather than pretending the six earned pairs had healed it. The current clinical guidance still applied. In the morning she chose a slower walk and no new overhead task. Living within a limit included unremarkable days when the limit was bothersome rather than dramatically tested.

shoal_e17_town_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_19.text: At Bo's shop, the apprentice posted the actual paid hours available for the following week. A friend asked whether he would remain forever. He said forever was an expensive word for a narrow current job. Bo heard and agreed. The business could want him to stay without owning his future. The apprentice could enjoy teaching Bo about the old drawer error without surrendering better work if a real offer came.

shoal_e17_town_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_20.text: Jin sent an ordinary note asking Yue to return a borrowed little rule at the next convenient offered visit. Yue had used it for a household question and almost forgotten it in her notebook cover. She returned it clean and apologized for the delay. The object was small, its ownership clear, and the correction simple. Not every mistake required a public account meeting to be admitted and put right.

shoal_e17_town_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e17_town_21.text: The partnership had begun considering a separately funded corrective task for current signal housings. Its ordinary receiving work would need a paid person, while qualified testing remained with qualified staff. Han asked whether Yue wanted to read the offer. She said yes, without accepting a scope not yet written. The possible work might support her remaining port stay, but tonight it was only a question to examine.
